topic: Teardown of Starboy (lilguy.net / CREATURE): site structure, voice, imagery, interactions, commerce, platform, strengths and weaknesses, and what SOUL must beat (fetched 2026-10-09)

findings.point: PLATFORM: lilguy.net is not a Shopify theme. It is one hand-built HTML page served by a Node/Express app on Railway behind Cloudflare. The response headers show `x-powered-by: Express`, `x-railway-edge: jfk1`, `server: cloudflare` and `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`. Shopify is used headless, for cart and checkout only. The store is named "CREATURE" (city New York, currency USD) at ipagrb-6a.myshopify.com, with checkout.lilguy.net as its domain. It runs the free Horizon theme 3.3.1 (theme_store_id 2481), has Shop Pay and Shop Pay Installments switched on, accepts Visa/Mastercard/Discover/Amex/Diners, and ships to about 240 countries including RO. hesjustalittleguy.com serves the same page from the same Express app. creature.company is a logo splash page plus the /eyes catalog.
findings.source: https://lilguy.net/ (response headers + page source); https://checkout.lilguy.net/meta.json; https://checkout.lilguy.net/ (Shopify.theme = Horizon 3.3.1); https://hesjustalittleguy.com/; https://creature.company/
findings.so_what_for_soul: Copy the architecture, not the theme. Keep SOUL's custom static landing (site/index.html, v2) as the brand front end. Use Shopify only as the backend: right now for waitlist customers and tags, and for checkout once CE is done. Do not move the brand site into a stock Shopify theme.

findings.point: STRUCTURE: everything lives on one URL with no header and no nav. The page runs in this order: a hero of 4 material renders with parallax and "when you wish upon a starboy."; then "he's just a little guy."; then one product paragraph of about 170 words; a live eye widget; "eye looks / view all 400" linking to creature.company/eyes; a grid of 13 product cards (10 body variants plus egg, dock and microbiner); a product-detail overlay; and a footer with Instagram, TikTok, X, an obfuscated contact email and a Dropbox press kit. /faq, /about, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml all return 404. No CTA or price appears above the fold. The first price is far down, in the grid.
findings.so_what_for_soul: SOUL v2 already has 13 sections: hold, born, colours, ai, claude, os, night, promises, boring bits, faq, reserve. Keep that depth and add what Starboy lacks. That means a slim sticky header with the Glass-O logo, an EN/RO switch and one "notify me" CTA, plus price and status visible in the first viewport. Give eyes, privacy, faq and specs their own linkable URLs or anchors so they can be shared and indexed.

findings.point: COPY VOICE: the copy is all lowercase (forced by CSS `text-transform: lowercase`), deadpan and affectionate, and it calls the device "he". Lines include "when you wish upon a starboy.", "he's just a little guy.", "bring him into a loud environment and he gets anxious. Leave him in the cold and he shivers. Shake him and he gets dizzy and mad at you", "flick him off if you feel like making him sad", "He is too dumb to know how to connect to your phone or the internet" and "built to the standard of a Swiss watch. It feels like a high-end piece of jewelry." The meta description is missing and og:description is just "⭐".
findings.so_what_for_soul: Their charm is the bar. SOUL's lines ("your ai has a brain. give it a soul.", "hold the glass.") are in the same register, so keep that voice. Beat them on clarity. Starboy's hero never says what the product is, what it costs or whether you can buy it. SOUL's first viewport should state all four: a palm-sized aluminium companion with living eyes; it works with your own Claude or ChatGPT, or offline; from €249; waitlist only, not on sale yet. Skip claims you can't prove, like "Swiss watch standard".

findings.point: IMAGERY: the site shows only studio renders on a light background. There are 4 large hero renders, one per material, at about 90–220 KB WebP each, and 24-frame 360° spins for every SKU and accessory. It has no lifestyle shots, no in-hand scale shots and no on-page video. preview.mp4 exists only as og:video for social previews.
findings.so_what_for_soul: SOUL has the context shots they lack: renders/v9 hand, desk, typing, family, side and ou_night, plus trailer/soul_trailer.mp4. Show the hand shot early for scale (90×101×31.5 mm). Embed the trailer as a poster with click-to-play and also set it as og:video. A per-colour 360° viewer is a nice extra, but only if real frames exist. Until then, swapping between the 5 colour renders is enough.

findings.point:
INTERACTIONS (excellent):
(1) The eye widget runs the device's real animation engine compiled to WebAssembly (animation_renderer.wasm 92 KB + anim_data.bin 14 KB) on a canvas. It cycles random looks every 3–6 s and follows the pointer. Clicking an eye opens that exact swatch in the catalog (creature.company/eyes?swatch=<shape>-<colour>).
(2) Every product card spins 360° on hover, with 24 frames packed into one .bin per SKU. On touch devices the spin follows scroll.
(3) A FLIP-style animation flies the product image from its card into a detail overlay.
(4) Headlines animate in character by character and "bump" on hover.
(5) A custom cursor morphs on hover.
(6) Text has a glitch effect.
findings.source: https://lilguy.net/eye_widget.js; https://lilguy.net/animation_renderer.wasm; https://lilguy.net/anim_data.bin; https://lilguy.net/glitch.js; inline scripts in https://lilguy.net/
findings.so_what_for_soul: This is the bar for SOUL's hero moment. SOUL already loads eyes/eyes.js and designs.js on the page. Make the web eyes the same engine as SoulOS and say so. Eyes should follow the pointer or finger, blink, react to scroll and sleep when idle. Tapping should show the design name and rarity. Each of the 120 designs needs a deep link (e.g. /eyes#<id>). Add one thing Starboy can't do: a "talk to it" demo using the SoulOS demo (os/index.html).

findings.point: EYE RARITY MECHANICS: the catalog is canvas-only, with the tagline "100 colorways. 4 shapes.", giving 400 looks. Odds are shown only as "% chance" text drawn on the canvas. Shapes: dot 10%, circle 40%, cat 30%, acorn 20%. Colourways are names like matcha, lobster, glowworm and starboy, split into 7 weight groups ranging from 1.90% down to 0.38% each. The rarest look is therefore about 0.04%. There are no named tiers. Each unit ships with a "unique mystery eye color". Press repeats different numbers: "over 5,000 eye combinations" and "5,000 facial expressions" against the site's 400.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
SOUL already has a stronger system: named tiers from Common 50% to Mythic 0.5%, 120 designs, 31 expressions, and a birth story derived from the chip id. Beat them on transparency and on shareability:
- Publish the odds table as real, accessible, indexable HTML, not canvas-only.
- Let people do a sample "birth roll" (v2 already has a roll with confetti) and share the result as an image or link.
- Keep the numbers identical on the site, the press kit and the packaging. Starboy's 400 vs 5,000 mismatch is exactly what to avoid.

findings.point:
VARIANTS & PRICES (USD):
- Painted diecast aluminium in Sunshine, Snow, Lilac, Magenta and Azure: $139.
- Anodized Aluminum: $249, includes the egg.
- Crystal (optical acrylic): $299.
- Stainless steel: $349.
- Brass: $399.
- Diamond Finish Aluminium: $599, "limited edition – 100 units".
- Add-ons: a brass halo checkbox at +$40 (only on CNC variants). The egg (raw aluminium plus silicone insert) is $60 on Shopify but "TBD / coming soon" on the site. A USB 3.1 1M cable is $24, sold out. The dock and the "cc microbiner" carabiner are "coming soon" with price TBD.
- Spec list on every variant: 400x400 OLED, camera, microphone, accelerometer, haptics, "24+ hours battery life", USB-C (cable included).
The whole line is pre-order.
findings.source: https://checkout.lilguy.net/products.json; window.__lgLive and productData in https://lilguy.net/ source; https://checkout.lilguy.net/collections/all
findings.so_what_for_soul: Their $139→$599 ladder anchors the $249 aluminium model as the sensible choice. SOUL's "from €249" sits right on Starboy's flagship aluminium price, so the page must justify that parity with what Starboy lacks: real conversation through the owner's own Claude or ChatGPT, on-device SOUL Memory, Maps and apps, hotspot roaming, and no camera. Show what's in the box and accessory prices only once they're decided. Use "price at launch" rather than Starboy's unfinished-looking "TBD".

findings.point: PRE-ORDER / SCARCITY: each detail panel lists "batch 1 – sold out" and "batch 2 – sold out" struck through, with "batch 3 – ships december 2026" in bold. The server stamps live inventory into the HTML (window.__lgLive.inv). At fetch time it showed e.g. sunshine 621, snow 769, alu 577, diamond 60, stainless 4, and magenta, crystal and brass at 0. A "(N left)" label appears only below 10 units. A SKU without a stamped buy link renders as "sold out", has no checkout URL anywhere in the page, and shows a waitlist email field instead.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
Live, honest scarcity sells. SOUL can't take money before CE, so borrow the mechanic without the payment:
- Collect "notify me" per colour (v2's colour select already does this).
- Plan a batch-based launch for later.
- Never show invented counters or "only N left" before launch.
- The rule "no payment link exists anywhere until sale opens" is good practice to state openly.

findings.point: CHECKOUT FLOW: the "pre-order" button goes to lilguy.net/checkout/{sku}. That returns a 302 to a Shopify cart permalink, e.g. https://ipagrb-6a.myshopify.com/cart/40599391961217:1?channel=buy_button, so the visitor lands in Shopify checkout with one item and no cart page. UTM and custom lg_* attribution parameters are appended on the way. Sold-out SKUs (/checkout/magenta) silently redirect to the homepage. Prices are geo-stamped ("country":"US") and formatted with Intl.NumberFormat in local currency through Shopify Markets, which lists RON for Romania and EUR for the EU.
findings.so_what_for_soul: Once SOUL is CE-certified, use the same pattern: a one-tap cart permalink into a branded Shopify checkout in EN or RO, priced in EUR with VAT shown (RON for Romania). Until then the same button posts to the waitlist. Closed states should say why ("not on sale yet — CE testing in progress") instead of silently redirecting.

findings.point: WAITLIST: the email field appears only for sold-out or coming-soon items. It POSTs to /api/subscribe with {email, material, variant, coming_soon_product}. There is no consent checkbox, no privacy link and no visible double opt-in. The placeholder "enter email for waitlist" is the only label.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
SOUL v2 is already better here: consent checkbox, honeypot, aria-invalid, and eyes that react while you type. Finish the job:
- Wire CFG.WAITLIST_ENDPOINT to a Shopify customer create.
- Set emailMarketingConsent with double opt-in.
- Add tags: waitlist, soul-m, colour-<x>, lang-en/ro, src-<utm_source>.
- Send a confirmation email in the visitor's language.
That makes it GDPR-clean, which Starboy's waitlist is not.

findings.point: ATTRIBUTION ENGINEERING (a hidden strength): the page captures referrer, utm_*, ?ref=<creator> (mapped to utm_content), and the in-app browser from the user agent. It recognises TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Threads, WeChat, Line, Discord and the Google app. It keeps the last touch for 24 h and the first touch for 90 days in localStorage. Its own domains (lilguy.net, creature.company, hesjustalittleguy.com, hesjustalilguy.com, littleguy.net) count as the same visit. All of it is forwarded to checkout and saved on the cart. This is clearly a creator- and TikTok-driven acquisition machine.
findings.so_what_for_soul: SOUL v2 currently sends only source:"landing-v2". Add the same first-touch, last-touch, ?ref= and in-app capture to the waitlist payload and store it as Shopify customer tags or metafields. You'll know which creator or channel brings signups before spending on ads, and ?ref= links let you run a creator programme from day one.

findings.point:
TRUST GAPS (Starboy's biggest weakness):
- No dimensions, weight or water resistance anywhere.
- No FAQ, no "how it works", no warranty.
- The Shopify refund policy and Terms of Service both return 404, even though the privacy policy references the ToS.
- The shipping policy is one sentence: "All items are pre-order and ship in November 2026".
- The privacy policy (updated July 8, 2026) is Shopify's generic template and says nothing about the device's camera or microphone.
- The main site shows no legal entity or address. Only the Shopify meta has "CREATURE, New York".
- No reviews.
This is for prepaid products costing $139–$599.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
This is SOUL's biggest opening. Publish, in EN and RO:
- Dimensions 90×101×31.5 mm, with weight and battery as [TBD] until measured.
- A plain data map: memory lives on the device and goes only to the AI you connect.
- "No camera. No always-on listening." as a headline promise.
- Company identity: ARTEMIS DIGITAL S.R.L., Bucharest.
- An honest CE line: "not yet CE-certified; we won't take payment until it is."
- The EU statutory rights that will apply at sale: 14-day withdrawal and the 2-year legal guarantee.
v2's "promises, in writing" and "the boring bits" are the right containers. Make them complete and linkable.

findings.point:
INCONSISTENT FACTS & SLIPPING DATES:
- The Shopify product and shipping policy say "SHIPS IN NOVEMBER 2026". The site's detail panels say batch 3 "ships december 2026" (magenta says november).
- March 2026 press cited a "September 2026" target.
- The egg is $60 on Shopify but "TBD" on the site.
- Magenta is available on Shopify but sold out on the site.
- Eye counts: 400 on the site vs 5,000+ in press.
- The AI story conflicts: "does not utilize large language models" vs "AI-powered companion".
findings.so_what_for_soul: Keep one source of truth: a single facts JSON for prices, dates, counts and status that feeds the EN/RO site, Shopify, the press kit and emails. Show a dated public timeline (prototype → CE testing → orders open → shipping) with a visible changelog when anything moves. A date that changes silently erodes trust, and Starboy is doing exactly that.

findings.point: RAW SHOPIFY STORE EXPOSED: checkout.lilguy.net serves the unbranded default Horizon theme. It shows the placeholder announcement "Welcome to our store", Home/Catalog/Contact navigation, a generic contact form (Name/Email/Phone/Comment), and a filterable /collections/all with EGG $60, STARBOY $249, STARBOY HALO and USB 3.1. /products.json is also public. This breaks the premium illusion and offers variants the main site marks as sold out.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
When SOUL's Shopify goes live:
- Password-protect the Online Store channel or redirect it to the landing page, so only checkout is public.
- Brand the checkout: Glass-O logo, brand colours, Bricolage Grotesque and Martian Mono.
- Remove default pages and placeholder copy.
- Keep products unpublished until CE is done.

findings.point:
ACCESSIBILITY FAILURES:
- The viewport sets `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, which blocks pinch-zoom (WCAG 1.4.4).
- There is no `prefers-reduced-motion` despite parallax, per-character animation, spins and the glitch effect.
- No `:focus-visible`, and `outline: none` appears 4 times.
- A custom cursor hides the system cursor (`cursor: none` ×8).
- Product cards are click-only <div>s with no tabindex or role, so keyboard users cannot open a product or reach "pre-order".
- The whole page has one aria-label.
- The eye catalog is canvas-only with no text alternative.
- Text is forced to lowercase.
findings.so_what_for_soul: SOUL v2 already uses prefers-reduced-motion, focus-visible and aria-labelledby on every section. Keep zoom enabled. Make colour and eye pickers real buttons or radios. Give the eyes canvas a live text alternative (e.g. "eyes: <design>, <rarity>, looking left"). Never hide the cursor. Don't claim "accessible" until a WCAG audit is done.

findings.point: PERFORMANCE: the HTML is 195 KB (35 KB compressed) with `cache-control: no-cache`. On load the page eagerly fetches every spin-frame bin, whether or not the visitor ever hovers: - 10.9 MB for the 11 bodies plus the egg, and 1.6 MB for accessories. - After 3 s, another 4.05 MB of brass-halo bins. - That is about 16.6 MB of frames. Add to that about 610 KB of hero renders, 2 × 100 KB OTF fonts (not WOFF2) and 92 KB of WASM. None of the 24 tags use loading="lazy". This is heavy for mobile data and for TikTok/Instagram in-app browsers, which is where their traffic comes from.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
SOUL v2 references about 0.57 MB of media plus 110 KB of HTML, roughly 25× lighter. Protect that lead:
- Set a budget: under 1.5 MB first load and LCP under 2.5 s on 4G.
- Lazy-load the trailer and secondary renders.
- Load any future 360° frames only on interaction.
- Fonts as WOFF2 with display=swap.
- Test inside the TikTok and Instagram in-app browsers.

findings.point:
SEO & SHARING:
- No meta description, canonical, robots.txt, sitemap, JSON-LD or hreflang.
- The <title> is "starboy – CREATURE" and og:description is "⭐".
- og:url points to hesjustalittleguy.com, which serves an identical page, so the same content lives on two domains.
- Everything sits on one URL, so products and eyes can't be deep-linked from the main site.
- The name "starboy" collides with The Weeknd's album, whose listings flood search results.
- One plus: og:video (preview.mp4) gives rich social previews.
findings.source: https://lilguy.net/ (head); https://hesjustalittleguy.com/; web search for "starboy lilguy" returning The Weeknd listings
findings.so_what_for_soul:
Fixes for SOUL:
- v2's og:image is relative ("media/soul-m-hero.jpg"). It must be an absolute https URL or social cards will break.
- Add og:video (the trailer), a canonical URL, hreflang for en and ro, a sitemap, and Organization + Product JSON-LD (no Offer until it's on sale).
- "SOUL" is also a generic word, so always pair it with a descriptor in titles (e.g. "SOUL — the AI companion with living eyes").
- Pick one canonical domain.

findings.point: POSITIONING: Starboy is an offline wearable digital pet. The site says it is a "completely standalone device… too dumb to know how to connect to your phone or the internet", and press says it does not use LLMs. It senses the world through a camera, microphone, temperature sensor and accelerometer, takes gestures ("give him a thumbs up to check the battery level"), and units "swap eyes, spread behaviors, and play with each other" when they meet "in the wild". It is worn with a halo or carabiner, positioned as jewellery.
findings.so_what_for_soul:
SOUL is the opposite on the main axis. It actually talks back, through the owner's own Claude or ChatGPT, or works offline. Its memory lives on the device. It has no camera and no always-on listening. Make the contrast without naming Starboy:
- "it talks back — with the AI you already have".
- "no camera. ever." Starboy has a camera and microphone with zero privacy explanation, which is a vulnerability SOUL's privacy story exploits directly.
- Only add a "meet another SOUL" social mechanic if the firmware really supports it.

findings.point: SOCIAL PROOF & PRESS: the footer links Instagram, TikTok and X (@lilguynet) and a Dropbox folder labelled "press kit". twitter:creator is @dankuntz. The site itself has no press logos, quotes, reviews or user content. Outside press includes Design Compass (27 Mar 2026), PAP Magazine (25 Jul 2026) and KultureGeek; the first two are promotional and uncritical, and I did not read the KultureGeek article.
findings.so_what_for_soul: SOUL v2 has no social links at all. Add the handles and build a real press page instead of a Dropbox link. It should carry the logo SVGs from brand/SOUL-Brand-Package, the 5 colour renders, the trailer, a one-page fact sheet generated from the single-source JSON, and a founder contact. Use [PRESS QUOTE] placeholders until real coverage exists. Never fabricate quotes or logos.

findings.point: MOBILE: breakpoints sit at 600, 768 and 1200 px. On touch devices the hover spin becomes a scroll-driven spin, the custom cursor is turned off, and the detail overlay gets a dedicated mobile CTA. But zoom is blocked, the page pulls about 17 MB, there is no sticky CTA on a long page, and nothing is lazy-loaded.
findings.source: https://lilguy.net/ (CSS @media rules; isTouchDevice spin logic; detail-mobile-cta)
findings.so_what_for_soul: On mobile, add a sticky bottom "notify me" bar that hides near the form, keep tap targets at least 44 px, and make the eyes respond to tap and drag. Check the colour picker and waitlist form inside the TikTok and Instagram in-app browsers, where most traffic will land.

findings.point: LOCALISATION: all copy is English and forced to lowercase. Only currency is localised, through Shopify Markets: RON for Romania and EUR across the EU, with prices formatted via Intl. There is no VAT or duties statement and no EU legal information.
findings.so_what_for_soul: SOUL's English default plus full Romanian (v2 already uses data-i18n) is a real advantage in Romania and the EU. Once selling, show EUR "incl. VAT" (RON for Romania), shipping and delivery in plain words, and EU consumer-rights copy in both languages.

summary:
I fetched and read the Starboy site on 2026-10-09: lilguy.net, its scripts and its assets, the eye catalog on creature.company, the hesjustalittleguy.com mirror, and the Shopify storefront and policies on checkout.lilguy.net. No checkout was completed and no email was submitted. I also compared it against SOUL v2 at /home/user/obsidian-vault/micul-smecher/site/index.html.

**What Starboy is, technically.** lilguy.net is one hand-built page on Node/Express (Railway, behind Cloudflare). Shopify is used headless for checkout only: store "CREATURE", ipagrb-6a.myshopify.com, free Horizon 3.3.1 theme, Shop Pay Installments on. "Pre-order" goes to /checkout/{sku}, which redirects to a Shopify cart permalink. Live stock is stamped into the HTML by the server. Sold-out items swap the button for a per-product waitlist that posts to /api/subscribe. The page also tracks first- and last-touch attribution, ?ref= creator links and the in-app browser (TikTok, Instagram, etc.), which points to creator-led TikTok marketing.

**What they do well:**
- The site runs the device's real eye engine in the browser (WebAssembly). The eyes follow the pointer, and clicking one opens that exact eye in the catalog.
- Every product spins 360° on hover and flies into a detail view.
- The eye catalog shows the exact odds of every look.
- The price ladder runs from $139 to $599 and makes the $249 aluminium model look like the sensible pick.
- Scarcity is real: sold-out batches are struck through, and "(N left)" appears only under 10 units.
- The lowercase, deadpan voice is charming and memorable.

**Where they are weak:**
- **Trust:** no specs, FAQ or warranty. The refund policy and Terms of Service both return 404. The shipping policy is one sentence. The privacy policy is Shopify's template and never mentions the device's camera or microphone. No company address appears on the main site.
- **Inconsistent facts:** the ship date slid from September to November to December 2026. The egg is $60 on Shopify but "TBD" on the site. Eye counts are 400 on the site but 5,000+ in press.
- **Exposed store:** anyone can browse the raw "Welcome to our store" Shopify site.
- **Accessibility:** pinch-zoom is blocked, there is no reduced-motion support, there are no focus styles, the system cursor is hidden, and product cards can't be reached by keyboard.
- **Weight:** about 17 MB downloads on every visit, mostly spin frames nobody asked for.
- **SEO and sharing:** no meta description, canonical, sitemap or structured data; og:description is just "⭐"; the same page lives on two domains; and the name "starboy" collides with The Weeknd's album in search.
- **Hero:** no navigation, and no price or call to action above the fold.

**What SOUL must beat, and how:**
1. **Live eyes on the page:** run the same engine as SoulOS, with eyes that follow the pointer or finger and a shareable sample birth roll. Each of the 120 designs needs a deep link.
2. **Rarity:** publish the named tiers (Common 50% to Mythic 0.5%) as an accessible HTML odds table, with the same numbers everywhere.
3. **Trust:** this is the biggest opening. Publish dimensions 90×101×31.5 mm; ARTEMIS DIGITAL S.R.L., Bucharest; "no camera, no always-on listening"; memory that stays on the device; an honest "not yet CE-certified, no payment until then"; the EU 14-day withdrawal and 2-year guarantee that will apply at sale; and a dated timeline with a changelog.
4. **One source of truth:** a single facts JSON feeding the EN/RO site, Shopify, the press kit and emails.
5. **Shopify:** for now use it only as the waitlist backend. Create customers with double opt-in consent and tags for colour, language and source (including UTM and ?ref=). Keep the storefront password-protected, and brand the checkout once you sell.
6. **Speed:** v2 is about 0.68 MB, roughly 25× lighter than Starboy. Keep a budget of under 1.5 MB first load and LCP under 2.5 s on 4G.
7. **Accessibility:** keep v2's reduced-motion support, focus styles and ARIA labels. Keep zoom enabled and add a text alternative for the eyes.
8. **Sharing fixes:** v2's og:image is a relative path and must become an absolute https URL. Add og:video from the trailer, canonical, hreflang en/ro, a sitemap and JSON-LD. Pair "SOUL" with a descriptor in titles.
9. **Social and press:** v2 has no social links yet. Add them, plus a real press page built from the brand package, renders and trailer, with [PRESS QUOTE] placeholders.
10. **Positioning:** state it in the first viewport, without naming Starboy: it talks back through the AI you already have, your memory stays on the device, there is no camera, from €249, waitlist only.
